newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT - MOTORCYCLING - Slight slips from superbike lead in Spain.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT - MOTORCYCLING - Slight slips from superbike lead in Spain.

text.p: WELLINGTON, Oct 7 - Kiwi superbike ace Aaron Slight has lost the lead in the world superbike champs and needs a minor miracle to take the title at the final round in Australia in three weeks, NZPA reported on Monday.
Sliqht's great rival Troy Corser of Australia scored a perfect double win at today's two legs in Albacete, Spain, leapfrogging the New Zealander who could do no better than ninth and sixth.
Battling flu symptoms all weekend, Slight had the added difficulty of lost grip in the rear tyre of his Castrol Honda and did well to fight through from 11th qualifying spot.

Corser meanwhile qualified on pole and flew unchallenged to his two victories. The factory Ducati rider now needs just fourth and fifth places to wrap up the championship at Phillip Island on October 27.

He has a commanding 353 points, while Slight advanced to 327 in Spain and now has another Ducati rider John Kocinski breathing down his neck. The American has 317 ahead of Sliqht's Castrol Honda team-mate Carl Fogarty (UK) on 308.

"The championship is not over for me yet but it's an uphill struggle -- I'll be giving it everything at Phillip Island," said the plucky New Zealander, the only rider to finish every race in this year's title chase.
Slight has finished third in the championship the past three years, last year Corser was second with neither of them able to approach Fogarty who was then riding a Ducati.
Kocinski recorded a second and third today, swapping placings with fellow American Colin Edwards (Yamaha).
Another Kiwi Simon Crafar finished fourth in both legs on his Kawasaki.
They were the Pukekohe based rider's best results in the series since the third round of the championships in May.
"I'm looking forward to the final round at Phillip Island," he said.
"The improved handling should help and the Dunlop tyres will hopefully run well again," he said of his bike fine-tuned by Japanese engineers.

Indifferent starts in both the Albacete heats meant Crafar had to come from behind to claim the two fourth places. In the first race he was 10th at the end of the first lap, having started seventh from the grid.
He picked the field one by one, including Slight to reach fourth spot.
In the second race Crafar again had to overcome Slight and Fogarty.
